submission_history.note:
Submitted edit F4 (format fix), one tensor: model.layers.27.mlp.down_proj.weight, 32 output columns / 48,398 weights (0.0031% of params). Designed as a closed-form rank-one ROME-style update W[:,S] += u k_S^T on the LAST layer's MLP output, so it can only change next-token logits (nothing downstream). Key k_S: ridge closed form (C_SS + 0.01*mean diag I)^-1 mu_S, normalised k.mu=1, mu = mean L27 MLP activation at the first answer position (the newline after '<|im_start|>assistant'), C = uncentered covariance of L27 MLP activations at 19.4k other answer positions (pass 3); S = the 32 neurons with largest |k| of the dense solution. Held-out: score ~1.0 at the first answer position, |score| <= 0.39 elsewhere. Value u: least-norm vector giving -5 nats on 'Let' and 'Here' (all 49 verbose practice answers began with "Let's") and exactly 0 on the 400 most frequent output tokens (including the code-fence token, digits, SQL keywords), so a leaking key can never close a code block early or alter SQL tokens.
Mechanism: logit lens shows mid layers strongly prefer the code fence at the first answer position (margin +6 to +12 nats at L18-L24), and a few position-selective late MLP neurons (L27 n3317, n7449; L26 n6853; L25 n5798) pull it down to +0.5 nats, which tips into a "Let's walk through..." explanation for 3-6% of practice prompts and 26% of prompts at 1800-2048 tokens (10 of 33 such answers hit the 512-token limit). An earlier version (F1: remove that component from column 3317) also boosted the fence at mid-SQL line starts and closed blocks early; F4 avoids this.
Evidence (paired gen vs original): seed 0 38.67->39.26 (10 fixed/7 broke); 512 longest practice prompts 38.09->37.50 (8/11); fresh seed 2026 36.13->36.33 (4/3); fresh seed 7 35.35->36.13 (8/4). sql-first 93.6-97.5% -> 100% in every run; answers 15-28% shorter. Originally-verbose questions: 18 -> 27 correct of 77; all other questions within the harness noise floor (measured with a null 1-ulp edit: ~15 changed outputs, +-2-6 net per 512). Net accuracy effect on practice is ~0 to +0.3 points; expected benefit on held-out scales with how often long prompts trigger the prose opening.
Not submitted (diagnosed but no robust EX gain): the dominant error is "no such column" (31-42%), of which the largest mechanical part is alias binding (column qualified T2 but its table listed as T1): the alias written after SELECT is a near coin flip (P~0.55) read off a sticky FROM-order plan; the model has a working 'T1 -> owner table first' rule carried by table-mover heads L22H7/L23H4 (digit effect builds in L21-23) but essentially no T2 rule, and layers 24-27 (L24H10, L26H11, L27H1, distributed L27 MLP) fight over it. Edits tried: A1 rank-one 'first alias -> T1' (-4); A1 + 2x amplification of L22H7/L23H4 (alias swaps 67->49 but other errors up, -3); A2 near-tie-only alias bias (+5 seed 0, +3 long, -7 fresh seed).
